script: Spread and total were not saved for Week 3 ARI@SF, so this script is form-only off two games. San Francisco's skill output is the more explosive one — Mike Evans 103 receiving yards, George Kittle 92, Demarcus Robinson 84 — and Brock Purdy is +0.98 EPA per dropback vs blitz, while Jacoby Brissett is -0.31 EPA vs blitz into a 49ers blitz rate of 28%. That leans SF toward sustained drives and Arizona toward Trey McBride (23 targets, 136 yards) rather than a shootout or blowout the missing number could confirm.
who_goes_off: George Kittle (9 targets, 92 yards, 88 air yards) and Mike Evans (10 targets, 103 yards, 95 air yards) are the 49ers built to stress Arizona's middle (9.53 YPA on 15 attempts) and right side (8.62 YPA on 24 attempts). Arizona's own log already says Trey McBride (23 targets, 136 yards, 125 air yards) over Marvin Harrison Jr. (4 targets, 33 yards) and over Michael Wilson (14 targets, 74 yards on 133 air yards).
weak_spot: Arizona's real weak spot is the middle of the field, 9.53 yards per attempt on 15 throws, with the right side also at 8.62 on 24 attempts — linebackers, nickel, and safeties, not outside corners. San Francisco's middle is the sturdy zone at 5.75 YPA on 8 attempts, their right side is the relative leak at 7.83 YPA on 24 attempts, and they have allowed only 3 runs of 10-plus yards at 3.95 YPC.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for ARI@SF, so no injury bump is on this card. The usage already in the two-game log is the split that matters: Kaelon Black 21 carries for 90 yards next to Christian McCaffrey's 20 for 91, and Tyler Allgeier 22 carries for 71 next to Jeremy Love's 20 for 70.
qb_vs_blitz: Jacoby Brissett is -0.31 EPA per dropback vs blitz on 15 dropbacks and +0.13 with no blitz, so San Francisco's 28% blitz rate hits Arizona's unresolved deep air — Michael Wilson 133 air yards for only 74 receiving yards, Marvin Harrison Jr. 74 air yards on 4 targets. Brock Purdy is +0.98 EPA vs blitz on 18 dropbacks against +0.38 with no blitz, and Arizona blitzes only 21%, so pressure is not how ARI slows Evans, Kittle, or Deebo Samuel (11 targets, 79 yards).

picks.why: Kendrick Bourne has 11 targets and 86 receiving yards through Arizona's two games, 43.0 per game against a 23.5 line, on only 50 air yards (4.5 aDOT), so he is the short target that still gets fed when Brissett is -0.31 EPA into SF's 28% blitz.

Christian McCaffrey is at 91 rush yards plus 63 receiving yards through two games, 77.0 combined per game against a 100.5 rush+rec line, and Kaelon Black already has 21 carries for 90 to CMC's 20 for 91. Arizona has allowed 3.98 YPC and 6 runs of 10-plus, so the under is the committee and a line 23.5 yards above his pace, not a stuffed run front.
